**Instrument and parties**
First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Pupil Transportation and Transportation Fleet Maintenance Services Contract, entered into as of July 1, 2025 (the Effective Date), attached to and made part of the Contract dated July 1, 2022. Parties: TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT, a Michigan general powers school district, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098; and FIRST STUDENT, INC., a Delaware corporation, 191 Rosa Parks Street, Suite 800, Cincinnati, Ohio 45202. Agenda item 3.b, June 3, 2025 meeting. Document control stamp 282059785.v1.

**Renewal Term**
Under Section 2.2, the School District exercises its option to extend, with the Parties agreeing to modify Section 2.2 and extend for two (2) years, commencing July 1, 2025 and expiring June 30, 2027. Thereafter the District may extend by up to one (1) additional year on a year-to-year basis, subject to written approval in its sole and absolute discretion (the Extension Term). Extension Term rates are to be mutually agreed under Section 10.3. The Contractor is stated to have no expectation of a contract beyond the Renewal Term.

**Other amended terms**
Exhibit B is replaced in its entirety. Sections 19.1 and 19.2 (Notices) are amended: notices to the District go to the Superintendent, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, copy to Jeremy S. Motz, Esq., Clark Hill PLC, 220 Park Street, Suite 200, Birmingham, Michigan 48009; notices to the Contractor go to First Student, Inc., Attn: Area General Manager, 120 Hart Avenue, Troy, Michigan 48098, copy to FirstGroup American, Attn: General Counsel, 191 Rosa Parks Street, 8th Floor, Cincinnati, Ohio 45202. A Change In Law clause terminates the District's obligations if federal or state law makes payment of the Rates illegal, impracticable or impossible. Further modification requires a writing signed by both Parties; the Contract is ratified and reaffirmed except as modified, with the First Amendment controlling in a conflict; execution may be in counterparts.

**Exhibit B charges and rates (Transportation & Bus Maintenance Services)**

| Pricing parameter | # of Routes | 2025-2026 | 2026-2027 |
|---|---|---|---|
| General Education Route Daily Route Charge | 33 | $306.78 | $334.39 |
| Special Needs Route Daily Route Charge - In District | 17 | $454.93 | $495.87 |
| Special Needs Route Daily Route Charge - Out of District | 7 | $454.93 | $495.87 |
| Mid-Day Runs & Shuttles (hourly, if not attached to Route) | 24 | $78.33 | $85.38 |
| Special Needs Route Daily Route Charge - Summer | 20 | $379.63 | $413.80 |
| Extra-Curricular/Athletic Trips (per hour) | Varies | $69.91 | $76.20 |
| Transportation Aides (per hour) | | $33.63 | $36.66 |

Footnotes state the charges include all costs and expenses for maintenance services for the buses; the Special Needs Daily Route Charge includes Out-District and Wing Lake Routes; the General Education Daily Route Charge also includes Summer General Education Routes; and extra-curricular/athletic trips carry a 1-hour minimum charge. White Fleet maintenance labor rates (parts at cost) are left to be mutually agreed before services are performed.

**Pricing assumptions**
Daily Route Charges assume an average Daily Route Time of 6.0 hours per day per Route, measured gate to gate from the District's Transportation Facility. Pricing assumes 175 days per academic year of regular route service, with a 175-day Academic School Year Minimum; one free dry run per Route is provided before school year start-up. Snow days are billed at 80% of the Daily Route Charge when driver pay is documented, otherwise 40%; intermittent closures at 40%; extended closures beyond ten consecutive school days at 70% or 25% depending on driver employment status. The District supplies fuel. A route-volume change of 10% or greater is deemed material and triggers good-faith renegotiation.
2025_314_3_b_troy_first_amendment_to_ame.verbose:
The First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Pupil Transportation and Transportation Fleet Maintenance Services Contract is entered into as of July 1, 2025, designated the Effective Date, and is attached to and made a part of the Amended and Restated Pupil Transportation and Transportation Fleet Maintenance Services Contract dated July 1, 2022. The Parties are TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT, described as a Michigan general powers school district with an address of 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, and FIRST STUDENT, INC., a Delaware corporation with an address of 191 Rosa Parks Street, Suite 800, Cincinnati, Ohio 45202. All capitalized terms carry the meanings set forth in the Contract unless expressly noted. The recital states that the Parties desire to exercise a Renewal Term and to amend the Contract Rates and other terms and conditions. The item appears on the Troy Board of Education agenda as 3.b for the June 3, 2025 meeting. Each page of the instrument carries the document control stamp 282059785.v1, and the signature block provides unexecuted By / Its / Date lines for TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT and FIRST STUDENT, INC.

Section 1, Renewal Term of Contract, recites that pursuant to Section 2.2 of the Contract the School District desires to exercise its option to extend, provided that the Parties agree to modify Section 2.2 and extend the Contract for two (2) years, commencing July 1, 2025 and expiring on June 30, 2027, defined as the Renewal Term. Thereafter the School District has the option to extend by up to one (1) additional year on a year-to-year basis, subject to the written approval of the School District in its sole and absolute discretion, defined as the Extension Term. Rates for any Extension Term are to be mutually agreed in accordance with Section 10.3 of the Contract. Nothing requires the School District to exercise the option, and the Contractor is stated to have no expectation of a contract beyond the Renewal Term or any exercised Extension Term.

Section 2, Rates, provides that as of the Effective Date the Rates set forth in Exhibit B are updated and Exhibit B of the Contract is replaced in its entirety with the Exhibit B attached to the First Amendment. Section 3, Notices, amends Sections 19.1 and 19.2 in their entirety while leaving the remainder of Section 19 unchanged. Under amended Section 19.1, required notices to the School District go to the Superintendent, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Road, Troy, Michigan 48098, with a copy to Jeremy S. Motz, Esq., Clark Hill PLC, 220 Park Street, Suite 200, Birmingham, Michigan 48009. Under amended Section 19.2, required notices to the Contractor go to First Student, Inc., Attn: Area General Manager, 120 Hart Avenue, Troy, Michigan 48098, with a copy to FirstGroup American, Attn: General Counsel, 191 Rosa Parks Street, 8th Floor, Cincinnati, Ohio 45202.

Section 4, Change In Law, provides that if any federal or state law, rule, regulation or ordinance is enacted, modified or otherwise changed that would make the School District's payment of the Rates and fees illegal, impracticable or impossible to pay, the School District's obligations under the First Amendment and the Contract cease and are not in effect. Section 5 limits further modification to a written agreement signed by both Parties. Section 6 states in capitals that the Contract is ratified and reaffirmed and continues in full force and effect except as modified, and that in the event of a conflict the First Amendment controls. Section 7 permits execution in one or more counterparts, each an original and all together constituting one document.

Exhibit B, captioned Contractor's Pricing, opens with pricing assumptions and conditions. Daily Route Charges are billed per Route per day; a Route includes the AM tier runs, Mid-Day or Shuttle runs if any, and PM tier runs operated by the same bus as part of the same Route package, and a Mid-Day or Shuttle run built into an AM/PM package is included in the daily Route charge while one not incorporated into a package is charged at the applicable listed rate. Daily Route Charges are based on an average daily Route time of 6.0 hours of service per day per Route, the Daily Route Time, calculated gate to gate from the School District's Transportation Facility. All Field Trips, Athletic Trips and Extra-Curricular Trips are calculated and invoiced on an hourly basis or portion thereof in quarter-hour increments.

The Contractor's pricing and fixed costs assume the School District operates school and requires regular route home-to-school transportation for 175 days per academic year for general education routing. The Contractor will conduct one (1) dry run for each Route in advance of school year start-up without charge. A 175-day Academic School Year Minimum applies to regularly scheduled Routes, with the academic year running from the first day of school in September until the last day of school in June and excluding summer transportation. The School District is not charged for Routes on days school is not in session or when Other Transportation Services are not operated, provided cancellation follows Section 10.1, subject to stated exceptions. For snow days, the School District is charged 80% of the Daily Route Charge for each Route not operated provided the Contractor demonstrates that all bus drivers are paid at their normal rate for their normally scheduled route; if the Contractor fails to pay or document such payment, the charge drops to the 40% rate. For intermittent closures, where the School District operates less than 180 per academic school year requiring Transportation Services because of power outages or similar intermittent events, the charge is 40% of the Daily Route Charge for each Route not operated less than 175 days.

Extended closures are defined as a period extending beyond ten (10) consecutive school days. Where the District replaces in-person instruction with hybrid or remote learning, it agrees to pay 70% of the then-current cost per Route per day for each Route not operated, provided that a qualified and trained bus driver is assigned and in active employment status receiving at least the driver's daily minimum pay rate; that all other Contractor staff positions, namely the Site Manager, Dispatcher and Router (the Management Personnel) and one (1) Mechanic (the Maintenance Personnel), remain in active employment status at full pay; that all wages are paid at prevailing or regular rates rather than a discounted hourly wage; and that the Contractor performs all other Transportation and Maintenance Services within contract parameters. If the Driver is not in active employment status receiving full pay, the rate is 25% of the then-current cost per Route per day. The School District may elect to operate under the 25% provision at its option during an extended closure. As a condition of payment, no later than five (5) days after each weekly or bi-weekly payroll cycle the Contractor must make available for inspection all books, records and data related to wages paid to personnel assigned to the School District; if verification shows terms were not met or that personnel are no longer employed, laid off or furloughed, charges are adjusted and the Contractor must reimburse overpayments. If the District operates under the 70% provision and also runs a food delivery program, athletic or extra-curricular routes or other auxiliary transportation, the Contractor uses staff from its to/from school or extra trips service team without additional fee unless services exceed contemplated parameters.

The Contractor's rates assume the School District provides the necessary fuel, and the Contractor is liable for all costs and expenses associated with misuse of that fuel. If changes to District operations cause a material increase or decrease in the volume of Routes, the Parties will convene and negotiate in good faith changes to Route Rates and Charges, with material defined as a change of equal to or greater than 10%. Adjustments to charges for any Extension Term follow Section 10.3.

The Charges and Rates schedule for Transportation & Bus Maintenance Services lists, by pricing parameter, number of routes and rate for 2025-2026 and 2026-2027: General Education Route Daily Route Charge, based upon 6.0 Daily Route Time, 33 routes at $306.78 and $334.39; Special Needs Education Route Daily Route Charge - In District, 17 routes at $454.93 and $495.87; Special Needs Education Route Daily Route Charge - Out of District, 7 routes at $454.93 and $495.87; Mid-Day Runs & Shuttles, hourly charge per run if not attached to a Route, 24 at $78.33 and $85.38; Special Needs Education Route Daily Route Charge - Summer, 20 routes at $379.63 and $413.80; and Extra-Curricular/Athletic Trips, charge per hour, quantity Varies, at $69.91 and $76.20. Footnotes state that these charges include all costs and expenses for maintenance services for the buses; that the Special Needs Daily Route Charge includes Out-District and Wing Lake Routes; that the General Education Daily Route Charge also includes Summer General Education Routes; and that extra-curricular and athletic trips carry a 1-hour minimum charge. Under Other Pricing Parameters, Transportation Aides are charged per hour at $33.63 for 2025-2026 and $36.66 for 2026-2027, while White Fleet maintenance, charged per hour for labor with parts at cost, is left blank with a note that labor rates will be mutually agreed to by the Parties prior to performing requested White Fleet Maintenance Services.

**Presentation**
Troy School District budget presentation dated June 03, 2025, presenter Dan Trudel, CPA. Contacts listed are dtrudel@troy.k12.mi.us and amalutan@troy.k12.mi.us, www.troy.k12.mi.us, 4400 Livernois Rd., Troy, MI 48098. The overview covers truth in taxation and establishment of millage rates; the General Fund (2024-2025 final amendments and 2025-2026 proposals); ancillary funds (2019 Capital Projects, 2023 Capital Projects, Debt, Building Site & Sinking, Capital Maintenance); and special revenue funds (Food Service, Troy Career Center, Community Service, Troy Preschool, School and Student Activities).

**Taxable values**
Homestead is defined as a taxpayer's primary residence or non-commercial agriculture; non-homestead as business or rental property, secondary and vacation homes, and commercial agriculture. Taxable value increases are capped at the lesser of the rate of inflation or 5%. Reported values: 2024 homestead 3,479,524,110, non-homestead 1,854,916,690, total 5,334,440,800; 2025 homestead 3,652,141,670, non-homestead 1,962,763,980, total 5,614,905,650.

**Millage components**
State Education Tax of 6 mills is levied on homestead and non-homestead property toward the foundation allowance. The 18-mill operating millage is levied on non-homestead property. Hold Harmless is calculated annually from enrollment, taxable values and the foundation allowance and levied on homesteads; FY25 was 2.7294 mills. FY25 sinking fund was 0.9606 mills and debt was 6.1000 mills. The Headlee Amendment, approved by Michigan voters in 1978, rolls back millage rates so taxes do not increase more than the rate of inflation; the district must annually calculate rollbacks to the operating and sinking fund millages.

2025_319_6e_mhsaa_membership_resolution_.page:
**Form and association**
Michigan High School Athletic Association membership resolution for 2025-26, presented as item 6E on the June 17, 2025 Troy Board of Education agenda. The MHSAA is located at 1661 Ramblewood Drive, East Lansing, MI 48823, telephone (517) 332-5046. It is described as a voluntary, nonprofit corporation of public, private and parochial junior high/middle and senior high schools whose boards of education or governing bodies have applied for and received membership on behalf of their secondary schools. Completed forms are to be saved and sent to camala@mhsaa.com as an attachment, with one signed copy returned and one retained.

**Terms of membership**
The association sponsors statewide tournaments and makes eligibility rules for participation. Boards that wish to host or participate must join and agree to abide by and enforce MHSAA rules, regulations and qualifications on eligibility, game rules and tournament policies, procedures and schedules. Participation in MHSAA postseason tournaments is conditioned on high schools adhering to at least the minimum standards of Regulation I and the maximum limitations of Regulation II in all MHSAA tournament sports. MHSAA tournaments are the collective property of the association rather than of any individual member school, and the association reserves rights over publication information, exclusive arrangements for recognition and exposure, restrictive policies against exploitation and commercialization, proprietary interests, and the use of images or transmissions identifying officials, spectators, students, personnel and marks. Resolutions that are modified or supplemented with letters imposing additional conditions are rejected.

**Resolution language**
The resolution covers the year August 1, 2025 through July 31, 2026 and enrolls the named schools as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc. and to participate in its approved interschool athletic activities. The board delegates supervision and control of those activities to the Superintendent or designee, accepts the association's Constitution and By-Laws, and adopts the rules, regulations and interpretations in the current Handbook as minimum standards and as the governing code, agreeing to primary enforcement. The authorization is effective from August 1, 2025 until July 31, 2026 and may not be revoked during that period. A Record of Adoption block provides for the day and month in 2025, the governing body name, board secretary or designee signature, address, city and zip, and contact e-mail; all are blank.

**Eligibility rules for listed schools**
Under the MHSAA Constitution, high schools, junior high/middle schools and comparable schools may join provided the building has enrollment and onsite attendance of at least 15 students, whether grades 6 through 8 or 9, 7 through 8 or 9, or 9 or 10 through 12, and provided nonpublic schools qualify for federal income tax exemption as not-for-profit organizations. Schools may join at the 6th-grade level to reach the 15-student minimum whether or not 6th-graders participate. Districts are not required to hold junior high/middle school membership or to sponsor 6th-grade athletics. If a listed junior high/middle school sponsors a 6th-grade team in any sport or lets a 6th-grader play with 7th and 8th graders, all of Regulations III and IV apply to all 6th-graders in all sports involving 6th-graders on that school's teams; if no 6th-graders participate in a sport, MHSAA rules do not apply in that sport.

**Completed entry**
The school listing pages are largely blank templates for up to 15 high schools and multiple junior high/middle schools. The single filled entry is line 4 under member junior high/middle schools: SMITH MIDDLE SCHOOL, grade configuration 6-8, anticipated 2025-26 7th and 8th grade enrollment of 419, anticipated 2025-26 6th-grade enrollment of 184, with Yes marked for 6th-graders participating in at least one sport with 7th and 8th graders and grade levels for membership marked 6, 7 and 8.
2025_319_6e_mhsaa_membership_resolution_.verbose:
The Michigan High School Athletic Association 2025-26 membership resolution form appears as agenda item 6E for the Troy School District Board of Education meeting of June 17, 2025. The association's address is 1661 Ramblewood Drive, East Lansing, MI 48823, with telephone (517) 332-5046. The MHSAA is described as a voluntary, nonprofit corporation comprised of public, private and parochial junior high/middle and senior high schools whose boards of education or governing bodies have voluntarily applied for and received membership for and on behalf of their secondary schools. The association sponsors statewide tournaments and makes eligibility rules with respect to participation in MHSAA-sponsored tournaments in the various sports. Each board of education or governing body that wishes to host or participate in such meets and tournaments must join the MHSAA and agree to abide by and enforce MHSAA rules, regulations and qualifications concerning eligibility, game rules, and tournament policies, procedures and schedules. It is stated as a condition for participation in any MHSAA postseason tournaments that high schools adhere to at least the minimum standards of Regulation I and the maximum limitations of Regulation II in all MHSAA tournament sports.

The form asserts that MHSAA tournaments are the collective property of the MHSAA and not of any individual member school, and that the association reserves the right to promote and advance the membership's interests through publication information; exclusive arrangements to create recognition and exposure for school-sponsored activities; restrictive policies prohibiting exploitation and commercialization of MHSAA-sponsored tournaments; appropriate proprietary interests; and the use of images or transmissions identifying contest officials, spectators, and member schools' students, personnel and marks. To obtain membership the board of education or governing body must adopt the resolution for its junior high/middle and senior high schools; the resolution must be formally ratified and properly signed, with one signed copy returned to the MHSAA for its files and one copy retained. Resolutions that are modified in any way or supplemented with letters placing additional conditions on MHSAA membership or tournament participation are to be rejected. The form directs the user twice to save the document and send it to camala@mhsaa.com as an attachment.

The membership resolution itself is captioned for the year August 1, 2025 through July 31, 2026. It provides blanks for the schools under the direction of the board, the city or township, and the county, all within the State of Michigan, and states that such schools are hereby (A) enrolled as members of the Michigan High School Athletic Association, Inc., a nonprofit association, and (B) further enrolled to participate in the approved interschool athletic activities sponsored by that association. The board of education or governing body delegates to the Superintendent or designee the responsibility for the supervision and control of those activities, accepts the Constitution and By-Laws of the association, and adopts as its own the rules, regulations and interpretations, as minimum standards, published in the current Handbook as the governing code under which the schools shall conduct their program of interscholastic athletics, agreeing to primary enforcement of those rules, regulations, interpretations and qualifications. Schools that host or participate in association meets and tournaments must follow and enforce all tournament policies, procedures and schedules. The authorization is effective from August 1, 2025 and remains effective until July 31, 2026, during which period it may not be revoked. A note specifies that junior high/middle and senior high schools of the school system to be listed as MHSAA members and to receive MHSAA mailings during 2025-26 must be listed on the back of the form.

The Record of Adoption block states that the resolution was adopted by the board of education or governing body of named schools on a blank day of a blank month, 2025, and is so recorded in the minutes of that board's meeting. Signature lines are provided for the governing body name, board secretary signature or designee with a checkbox to indicate a designee, address, city and zip code, and contact e-mail. As presented, these lines are unfilled.

The reverse side, headed Schools Which Are To Be MHSAA Members During 2025-26, sets out eligibility conditions from the MHSAA Constitution. All high schools, junior high/middle schools, or other Michigan schools doing a corresponding grade of work may become members provided that the school building has enrollment and onsite attendance of at least 15 students, whether for grades 6 through 8 or 9, grades 7 through 8 or 9, or grades 9 or 10 through 12; and, if a nonpublic school, that the school qualifies for federal income tax exemption as a not-for-profit organization. To reach the 15-student minimum for middle school membership, schools may join the MHSAA at the 6th-grade level whether or not 6th-grade students participate in athletics. Paragraph A states that the section does not require school districts to become member schools at the junior high/middle school level and does not require districts to sponsor any interscholastic athletics for 6th-grade students. Paragraph B states that if a district's MHSAA Membership Resolution lists a junior high/middle school as a member school, and if that school sponsors a 6th-grade team in any sport or permits a 6th-grade student to participate with 7th- and/or 8th-grade students in any sport, then all of Regulations III and IV apply to all 6th-graders in all sports involving 6th-graders on teams sponsored by that school; if the school does not allow any 6th-graders to participate in a sport, MHSAA rules do not apply in that sport.

The listing pages provide numbered blanks for up to fifteen member high schools and separate blocks for member junior high/middle schools covering 6th, 7th and 8th-grade buildings, each block asking for the name of the member school, the configuration of grades in the building with examples K-6, 6-8, 7-8 and 7-9, anticipated 2025-26 7th and 8th-grade enrollment, anticipated 2025-26 6th-grade enrollment, grade levels for membership among 6, 7 and 8, and a yes/no indication of whether 6th-graders will participate in at least one sport with 7th and 8th graders, with a line for the building housing 6th-graders if not the same building. Instructions direct that junior high/middle schools be listed separately from high schools even where all grades are housed in the same building, and that additional schools be listed on a separate sheet if necessary.

Only one school entry is completed in the document as presented. Under member junior high/middle schools, line 4 names SMITH MIDDLE SCHOOL, with the configuration of grades in the building given as 6-8, the anticipated 2025-26 7th and 8th-grade enrollment given as 419, and the anticipated 2025-26 6th-grade enrollment given as 184. The Yes box is marked X for 6th-graders participating in at least one sport with 7th and 8th graders, with the line for a separate building housing 6th-graders left blank, and grade levels for membership are marked X for 6, X for 7 and X for 8.
